long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Flohr spent nearly two decades in computing and asset finance before becoming an entrepreneur. He says he saved his employment income to fund his own asset-finance company, then bought a business jet after finding private charter opaque and inconsistent. Strong charter demand for that aircraft led him to found VistaJet in 2004.

Flohr replaced aircraft ownership with a subscription model built around a floating global fleet, predictable pricing and consistent service. He later formed Vista Global to combine VistaJet, on-demand flying, technology, leasing and other aviation services. The group remains his defining business, and he serves as founder and chairman. Outside the boardroom, he has sustained a parallel competitive career in Ferrari endurance racing.

uncertainties.detail: SuperyachtNews directly interviewed Thomas Flohr and identified him simultaneously as VistaJet founder and owner of the 42-metre Baglietto Nina J. Forbes, Vista and FIA records align on the same Swiss business and racing identity, leaving no material namesake ambiguity.

The dedicated Forbes profile nonetheless identifies VistaJet as his wealth source and valued the aviation equity as the principal fortune, so Aviation & Aerospace is selected at slightly reduced confidence rather than Finance & Investments or Mixed.

Flohr told McKinsey he saved his employment income, avoided a large lifestyle and used his own equity to create his asset-finance company; he separately described coming from nothing.
